Leading Causes of Fort Lauderdale Truck Accidents Truck accidents can be catastrophic, which is why the trucking industry is heavily regulated by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration and Florida state law. Despite strict safety regulations, across the Sunshine State in 2020, hundreds of people were injured, and at least 29 were killed in accidents involving large trucks.Common causes of truck accidents include:SpeedingDriving too fast for road conditionsTruck driver fatigue (often due to spending too much time behind the wheel in violation of Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration hour of service regulations)Distracted drivingDrug and alcohol useTraffic congestionTruck driver being unfamiliar with local roads in Fort LauderdaleMerging errors, particularly on I-95 on- and off-rampsFailure to stopBraking errorsCargo shifts due to uneven cargo loadsFailing to look for other motorists, bicyclists, or pedestriansFailing to maintain a single laneUnsafe turnsDriving in a truck’s blind spotRoad constructionLimited visibilityBad weather conditionsVehicle defectsVehicle malfunctionsNegligent hiringFailing to perform required pre- and post-trip inspectionsFailing to perform necessary vehicle maintenance and repairsFailing to pull malfunctioning vehicles from the fleet of serviceOur truck accident attorneys in Fort Lauderdale will carefully examine the specific circumstances of your crash to identify every possible cause. Once we know why the accident happened, we can determine who is at fault and legally responsible for your injuries. Who is typically responsible for a commercial truck accident? Under Florida law, liability for a big rig truck accident is shared by everyone who plays a role in the crash. Depending on the specific facts of your case, liable parties might include:Truck driverTrucking company or serviceFreight brokerOwner of the tractor or trailerTruck maintenance companyNegligent third-party motoristMotorcyclistPedestrianBicyclistTruck manufacturerProperty ownerGovernment agencyMost often, trucking companies and their insurance companies will be liable for the consequences of a truck accident. You might not have the resources to take on these adversaries and win, but our Fort Lauderdale truck accident attorneys do.We have gone toe-to-toe with powerful corporations for years, winning top results for injured crash victims like you in the process. Call our law office in Fort Lauderdale so you can put yourself in the best position to win your case. Can I recover compensation if I’m blamed for a Florida truck accident? A negligent truck driver or trucking company might be quick to blame you for a collision. When this happens, being prepared to fight back is crucial. Florida has adopted a pure comparative negligence system, meaning your take-home financial award is impacted by the degree of fault you share.Let’s say you are involved in an accident with a tractor-trailer on I-95 in Fort Lauderdale. You suffer damages worth $500,000 and are assigned 10 percent of the blame for the collision. Once shared fault is taken into account, your financial recovery will be limited to $450,000. If you don’t stand up to shared liability claims, you could watch valuable compensation slip away.At Meirowitz & Wasserberg LLP, we witness victim-blaming tactics all too often. Our truck accident lawyers in Fort Lauderdale will be ready to implement tried-and-true strategies to limit how much, if any, blame you are assigned. Damages Available to Injured Truck Accident Victims in Fort Lauderdale The physical, emotional, and financial consequences of a truck accident in Broward County can be devastating. Fortunately, you are entitled to seek compensation if you were injured through little to no fault of your own. In Florida, truck accident victims can seek economic damages and noneconomic damages.Florida is a no-fault state, so your first step will be to file a claim for personal injury protection benefits with your insurance carrier.Personal injury protection benefits will cover 80 percent of your medical bills (up to $10,000) and 60 percent of your lost wages. If you are in a car accident involving a truck, your damages will likely exceed your personal injury protection benefits.If your injuries are classified as severe, you can then pursue compensation through a third-party insurance claim or lawsuit, which allows you to recover damages for:Medical expensesDisabilityLost job opportunitiesLost job benefitsLost incomeNursing assistanceRehabilitationPain and sufferingDepression and anxietyPost-traumatic stress disorderDisfigurementLoss of consortiumReduced quality of lifePunitive damages can also be awarded in a truck accident lawsuit, but only in cases where a defendant’s conduct was intentional or rose to a level of gross negligence.At Meirowitz & Wasserberg LLP, our Fort Lauderdale injury lawyers will carefully examine the details of your semi-truck accident with the help of respected experts and specialists. Their insights help us better understand your case and how the crash has impacted you. The more we know about how your life has changed, the better prepared we will be to secure a meaningful result on your behalf. How much is my Fort Lauderdale truck accident case worth? There is no standard settlement or value for a truck accident claim. Instead, the amount of money you can recover will depend on factors and details specific to your crash and life. Important considerations include:Your injuries, including the types and severityWhether you are able to continue workingChanges in your earning capacityHow your life has been impacted by the trauma of being hit by a tractor-trailerWhether the collision has aggravated a preexisting medical conditionYour ageShared responsibility for the truck accidentWhether you will require nursing care or personal care assistance while you recover (or for life)Choosing an experienced and respected Fort Lauderdale trial attorney can also help you maximize your financial recovery.Our attorneys at Meirowitz & Wasserberg LLP have secured millions of dollars in life-changing compensation for truck accident victims and grieving families across the nation. You can benefit from our experience, resources, and passion by calling our law office in Fort Lauderdale today to arrange a free consultation. Further, your medical record will document your trauma and provide proof that the crash caused your injuries, which is critical information in establishing negligence and winning compensation in a truck accident claim.
